question: Should OpenClaw support opt-in approval-bound execution from symlinked cwd paths, and if so must the approval explicitly show both the requested path and canonical target before the user approves it?
rationale: This is a new security-sensitive configuration contract rather than a repair to an established supported mode; the code can preserve an inode identity, but it cannot determine the intended user-consent presentation or acceptable trust scope without maintainer direction.

options.title: Adopt the canonical dual-path design
options.body: Keep the default denial, require an explicit opt-in, display requested and canonical cwd in the approval, and land only a rebased narrow implementation with real proof.

options.title: Reject the opt-in setting
options.body: Keep canonical-cwd enforcement unconditional and improve the denial guidance or supported canonical-path workflow instead.

recommendation.title: Adopt the canonical dual-path design
recommendation.body: Keep the default denial, require an explicit opt-in, display requested and canonical cwd in the approval, and land only a rebased narrow implementation with real proof.
